approach: Put the rule in one place in athena-git: `Git::own_origin_url(remote)` refuses any remote name but `origin`, requires `git remote get-url --all origin` and `git remote get-url --push --all origin` to each list exactly one URL, and requires both to name the same repository. `Git::push_branch` and `Git::push_if_remote_at` call it first. In crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs add `guard_origin_write(git, name)`, which wraps it, and call it first in `GitRemote::push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`; reads stay unguarded. The pull-request side is pinned the same way: `land_pr` (landing.rs:866) and `Athena::github_repository` (early.rs:363-366) read the origin URL through the checked read, so a doubled or mismatched origin yields no host call and no `GitRemote`. URL normalisation: strip scheme and userinfo, lower-case the host only, rewrite the scp colon only when there is no `scheme://`, drop a trailing slash and `.git`; path case and an explicit port are compared as written, so a difference is refused on purpose (fails closed). Tests use real git over temp bare `origin` and `upstream` repos; each first shows a plain `git push` to `upstream` succeeds (same user, same environment), then shows the guarded call refused with refs unchanged. docs/spec.toml gets the mechanism and a measure ending `status: not shown`; CHANGELOG.md gets one Unreleased line. Revision: dependents now cover test_support `land_through_pr`, the cli reconcile/binary/trailer_stop tests, the production checkpoint writer attribution.rs:785 and the read-only origin readers; the early.rs change gets a doubled GitHub origin test; the land_pr test claim is narrowed; normalisation is tightened; the lost git-push-failure coverage is restored with a pre-receive hook test in athena-git.

decisions.choice: Put the URL check in `athena_git::Git::own_origin_url` (athena-git/src/lib.rs) and have remote.rs `guard_origin_write` call it.
decisions.reason: athena-core depends on athena-git, not the reverse, and the records writer pushes through `Git::push_branch`/`push_if_remote_at` (records_branch.rs:401-459), which core's GitRemote never sees. One implementation covers both paths and criterion 2 names both files.

rejected.why: Records pushes (append_to_remote from attribution.rs:785, gh/records.rs:156 and 365, reconcile.rs:746 and 841, records_import.rs:206) would stay able to push to any named remote, so Athena's own publishing would not be bounded.

rejected.option: Duplicate the check in core and git
rejected.why: Two copies of a URL-identity rule can drift; one function is easier to show with a test.

decisions.choice: Refuse when `get-url --all` or `get-url --push --all` lists more than one URL, or when the two name different repositories. Error text never echoes a URL.
decisions.reason: A push goes to every push URL (the push URLs, else the fetch URLs); a doubled push URL, or a doubled fetch URL with no push URL, would publish to a second place. `get-url --push --all` falls back to the fetch URLs, so one pair of reads covers both. parse_remote's comment (client.rs:1194-1195) says URLs are not echoed because they may carry a credential.

rejected.why: It returns the first URL only; it misses a second push URL and a separate push URL.
Local-path origins (every test) are not GitHub URLs and parse_remote rejects them. The guard must work for any URL form, so it uses a generic normalisation.

decisions.choice: Normalisation rules (answers finding 4): rewrite the scp colon to a slash only when the URL has no `scheme://` (true `[user@]host:path` form); keep an explicit port in an https URL as part of the host; strip userinfo, a trailing slash and `.git`; lower-case the host only; compare the path case-sensitively. A difference in path case or in port presence is refused on purpose.
decisions.reason: Rewriting the colon after stripping the scheme would turn `https://github.com:443/o/r` into `github.com/443/o/r`. Both false-refusal cases fail closed (a refusal, never an extra write), and local paths are case-sensitive, so one rule for all URL forms is the smallest correct design. Unit tests show an https URL with a port equals the same URL with the same port, differs from the portless one, and that a case-differing path is refused.

rejected.option: Lower-case the whole URL or fold path case for GitHub
rejected.why: Local-path origins are case-sensitive; a GitHub-only fold needs a second code path and still only widens what is allowed.
It corrupts explicit ports and merges different URLs.

decisions.choice: The guard allows exactly the name `origin` and does not look for a separate list of allowed remotes.
decisions.reason: The brief's rule is 'the repo's own origin'; every production caller already passes the literal origin (landing.rs:865, early.rs:374-377 and 458-461, reconcile.rs:403, attribution.rs:510 DEFAULT_REMOTE, cli main.rs:1751, test_support.rs:620-645), so no production caller changes behavior.

rejected.option: A config key listing allowed remotes
rejected.why: It would touch athena.toml or defaults.toml, which are out of scope, and would let a setting widen the boundary.

(b) `git_remote_refuses_a_doubled_push_url_and_a_doubled_fetch_url`: origin first accepts a push (control); then `git remote set-url --add --push origin <second bare>` makes `push` Err with both bares unchanged; in a second repo `git remote set-url --add origin <second bare>` (two fetch URLs, no push URL) makes `push` Err with both bares unchanged. (c) `git_remote_refuses_a_push_url_naming_another_repository`: single `remote.origin.pushurl` on another bare; Err and unchanged. (d) `origin_repository_reads_only_the_parsed_owner_and_repo`: `own_origin_repository(git)` returns `example/project` for `https://github.com/example/project.git`, Err for no origin, Err for a local-path origin (parse_remote refuses non-GitHub), Err for an https origin with a second push URL on another repo; a `GhClient` on a ScriptRunner with that repository, calling `close_pr(9, ..)`, only reaches `repos/example/project/...` paths. (e) `a_local_path_origin_makes_no_host_or_remote_call` and `a_doubled_github_origin_makes_no_host_or_remote_call`: an `Athena` from `code_health::tests::set_up()` with the early seam holding an `EarlyFake` (test_support.rs:275). Local-path origin: `early_pr`, `push_ci_branch`, `delete_ci_branch` leave the fake's `calls` and `ci_calls` empty. Control: a single-URL origin `https://github.com/example/project.git` makes the fake record a push and an open_pr. Doubled: the same GitHub origin plus `git remote set-url --add --push origin <other url>`; the three calls leave `calls` and `ci_calls` empty. (f) `land_pr_builds_the_remote_and_sink_only_after_the_checked_origin_read`: `include_str!` of landing.rs; asserts the position of `own_origin_repository(` is before `GitRemote {` and before `GitLandingRecords::for_remote` in `land_pr`; its claim is ordering only (reconcile at landing.rs:842 runs earlier and is bounded by the athena-git guard, shown by the athena-git twin). Normalisation unit tests in athena-git/src/lib.rs: https vs scp-style same repo accepted; other repo refused; https with an explicit port equal to itself, refused against the portless URL; path case difference refused; and the pre-receive hook test: a single-URL bare origin whose hook exits 1 makes `push_branch` and `push_if_remote_at` return Err from git, refs unchanged. Also run `cargo test -p athena-git`.
demonstrations.observes: Every refusal case returns Err (or makes no call) and every ref listing is unchanged. A single-URL https origin yields only the parsed owner/repo, and the PR client builds paths only for it. The control makes the EarlyFake record calls, so empty calls in the doubled case mean refusal.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the single-URL and same-repo checks, the doubled-URL pushes succeed and one bare changes; without the checked read in `github_repository`, the doubled GitHub origin case makes the EarlyFake record a push and an open_pr; without `own_origin_repository`, a doubled origin would yield a repository.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `GitRemote` methods, `Git::own_origin_url`, `own_origin_repository`, `Athena::early_pr`/`push_ci_branch`/`delete_ci_branch` (early.rs:384-437, pub(crate), reached from the same crate; `with_ci_remote` takes the seam first at early.rs:369-373 but `github_repository` still reads git, which is what the doubled case tests). Fixtures: real temp bare repos; `ScriptRunner` (gh/tests.rs:4794, exists); `EarlyFake` injected through `gh::early_seam::install` (gh/mod.rs:99, exists, used at run_pin_tests.rs:425), guard held to the end of the test. `own_origin_repository`, `Git::own_origin_url` and the tests are added by plan steps 2 to 6. No double holds the logic under test.
